text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- According to the final 1995 census results, Macedonia has 1,924,932 ihabitants out of which 66.6 percent are Macedonians, 22.8 percent ethnic Albanians, four percent ethnic Turks, 2.2 percent ethnic Romes, 2.1 percent Serbs and 0.4 percent Vlach people, director of the republic's statistics office Svetlana Antonovska says.

- Macedonian foreign minister Ljubomir Frckovski said that almost two thirds of the countries which had established diplomatic relations with the republic had recognised it by its constitutinal name Macedonia.

- Macedonia will soon finalise three-years ESAF loan with the annual interest rate of 0.5 percent. This will be a third International Monetary Fund credit to the republic which by now has already received loans at the value of $75 million.
- Macedonia will assume flight control over its air space on November 8.
- Macedonia's annual inflation rate of four percent is among the lowest in 36 East European countries.
